overview: Surendrapuri — Kunda Satyanarayana Kaladhamam, located at the foothills of Yadagirigutta in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana, is India's first mythological theme park and religious tourism destination, spread over 17 acres. Opened to the public in May 2003 by Sri Kunda Satyanarayana (in memory of his late son Surendra), the complex features 3,000+ sculptures across a 3-km pathway, organised into four categories: Temples of India (life-size replicas of 100+ famous Indian temples), Epics of India (Ramayana, Mahabharata, Bhagavata, Buddha Charita), Puranas (Ksheera Sagara Madhanam, Gajendra Moksham, Padmavyuham, Kurukshetra War, etc.), and Saptalokas (the 7 celestial worlds — Brahmalok, Vishnulok, Shivalok, Nagalok, Indralok, Narakalok/Yamalok, Patalalok). The complex also houses the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam (16-foot black-stone Panchamukha Hanuman from Kanchi + Mahashivalinga similar to Pasupatinath Nepal), 9 Navagraha Temples (each planet with its consort and vahana in dedicated temples), Nagakoti (a 101-foot Shivalinga atop Nagadri Hill encircled by Kaalasarpa with 10 million small anthill-mud Shivalingas), and Surendrapuri's iconic 60-foot double-sided Panchamukha Hanuman-Shiva statue at the entrance. ~60 km from Hyderabad; 10 km from Bhuvanagiri Railway Station; 2 km from Yadadri Bus Terminal. Entry: Adult ₹350, Child (5–10 yrs) ₹300, below 5 years free. Open daily 9 AM – 5:30 PM (visiting 9 AM – 7 PM).
summary: Surendrapuri — Kunda Satyanarayana Kaladhamam, in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana, is India's first mythological theme park and religious tourism destination, spread over 17 acres at the foothills of Yadagirigutta. Opened in May 2003 by Sri Kunda Satyanarayana (in memory of his son Surendra), the complex features 3,000+ sculptures across a 3-km pathway in 4 categories: Temples of India (life-size replicas of 100+ famous Indian temples), Epics of India, Puranas, and Saptalokas. It also houses the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam (16-foot black-stone Panchamukha Hanuman from Kanchi + Mahashivalinga), 9 Navagraha Temples, the 101-foot Nagakoti Shivalinga (with 10 million small anthill-mud Shivalingas), and a 60-foot double-sided Panchamukha Hanuman-Shiva statue at the entrance. ~60 km from Hyderabad; entry Adult ₹350, Child (5–10 yrs) ₹300, below 5 years free; open daily 9 AM – 5:30 PM (visiting 9 AM – 7 PM). Designed and built by Satyanarayana Kunda and inaugurated as the Kaladhamam in February 2009 by the then-Governor of Andhra Pradesh, N.D. Tiwari.

history.content: Surendrapuri was conceptualized and built by Sri Kunda Satyanarayana, who was born in a small village near Khammam (Telangana) in an agricultural family whose modest means did not allow him to pursue a formal higher education. The sudden passing away of his youngest son, Surendra Babu, aroused in Sri Satyanarayana a desire to build something to keep his memory alive. The idea of a mythological park seemed apt due to his deep abiding love for Indian culture and traditions. He was confronted by daunting challenges — advancing age, huge project costs, and the dissuasion of friends and associates. All the deterrents only served to firm his resolve. At the age of 70, when people have generally retired, he worked doubly hard to bring his dream project to life. After over a decade of dedicated hard work and single-minded commitment, Surendrapuri took concrete shape. Today it stands as a testament to one man's vision, determination and never-say-die attitude.
history.foundation_year: Surendrapuri opened to the public in May 2003; the Kunda Satyanarayana Kaladhamam (the mythological museum) was inaugurated in February 2009 by the then-Governor of Andhra Pradesh, Narayan Dutt Tiwari

sthala_puranam: Surendrapuri does not have a traditional Sthala Puranam as it is a modern mythological theme park and religious tourism destination. The site's sacred character is derived from the 100+ life-size replicas of India's most revered temples (including Tirumala Balaji, Madurai Meenakshi, Kashi Viswanath, Rameswaram, Jagannath Puri, Golden Temple Amritsar, Somnath, Kedarnath, Guruvayur), the sculpted depictions of key events from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, Bhagavata, the life of Buddha, and key events from the Puranas (Ksheera Sagara Madhanam / churning of the ocean, Gajendra Moksham, Padmavyuham, Kurukshetra War, etc.), and the 7 celestial Saptalokas (Brahmalok, Vishnulok, Shivalok, Nagalok, Indralok, Narakalok/Yamalok, Patalalok). The complex also houses the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam (the protective avatara of Hanuman who killed the 5 bees that hid Mahi Ravan's life), the 101-foot Nagakoti Shivalinga (with 10 million small anthill-mud Shivalingas for Naga Dosha, Kuja Dosha and Kaalasarpa Dosha remedies), and the 9 Navagraha Temples. Surendrapuri is named after Sri Kunda Satyanarayana's son Surendra Babu, and the Kaladhamam is named after Sri Satyanarayana himself.
religious_significance: Surendrapuri is significant in three ways: (1) as India's first mythological theme park, providing an educational and devotional experience of Hindu epics, Puranas, and Saptalokas through 3,000+ sculptures across a 3-km pathway; (2) as a religious-tourism destination housing multiple temples, including the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam (with a 16-foot Panchamukha Hanuman from Kanchi and a Mahashivalinga similar to the Pasupatinath in Nepal), 9 Navagraha Temples (each planet with its consort and vahana), and the 101-foot Nagakoti Shivalinga; and (3) as a 'tirth yatra' in a single place — visitors can see life-size replicas of 100+ of India's most famous temples in one visit. It is highly relevant for planetary dosha remedies (Naga Dosha, Kuja Dosha, Kaalasarpa Dosha at Nagakoti; planetary shanti at Navagraha Temples) and for protective worship (Panchamukha Hanuman). It is usually visited in conjunction with the famous Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple at Yadagirigutta (3 km away), forming a popular weekend pilgrimage from Hyderabad.
spiritual_significance: Devotees believe that the 16-foot Panchamukha Hanuman at the temple protects them from evil and grants courage. The Panchamukha avatara is especially worshipped for protection from black magic, evil eye, and negative energies (since Hanuman, in this form, killed the 5 bees that hid Mahi Ravan's life — defeating all 5 forms of evil simultaneously). The 101-foot Nagakoti Shivalinga, encircled by Kaalasarpa, is believed to be so powerful that just by pradakshina (circumambulation) one can attain salvation from the ill-effects of Naga Dosha, Kuja Dosha and Kaalasarpa Dosha. The 9 Navagraha Temples are believed to mitigate the negative effects of planetary positions on a devotee's horoscope. The 10 million small anthill-mud Shivalingas at Nagakoti are believed to carry the divine energy of the main 101-foot Shivalinga. Many devotees also visit Surendrapuri as a comprehensive 'temple tour of India' — a unique way to gain familiarity with India's diverse temple architecture and mythology in a single visit.

Nagakoti pradakshina — remedy for Naga Dosha, Kuja Dosha, and Kaalasarpa Dosha (just by walking around the 101-foot Shivalinga)
Navagraha Temples — remedy for negative planetary positions in one's horoscope; shanti pujas and homas (especially Navagraha Homa for the eradication of evil)

miracles_and_devotee_experiences: The Panchamukha avatara of Hanuman is itself a miracle: Hanuman manifested this form to kill 5 bees that hid Mahi Ravan's life, saving Ram and Lakshman from his clutches.
The Panchamukha Hanuman holds 10 different weapons in his hands and has 5 different faces (Vanara, Narasimha, Garuda, Varaha, Hayagreeva) — a unique protective avatara.
The Panchamukha Shiva statue represents the Pancha bhootha and Pancha tatwa — the five elements and the five cosmic principles; his 5 faces are Sadyojatha, Vama deva, Aghora, Tatpurusha and Eeshana.
The 60-foot double-sided statue of Panchamukha Hanuman and Shiva at the entrance is one of the tallest religious statues in the Telugu-speaking states.
The 101-foot Shivalinga at Nagakoti is one of the tallest Shivalingas in India, encircled by the giant snake Kaalasarpa and accompanied by 10 million small Shivalingas made from anthill mud.
architecture: Surendrapuri is built across 17 acres of land, with a 3-km pathway marked by arrows that visitors follow in sequence. The architecture is a unique blend of devotional art, museum display, and temple construction. The complex is divided into multiple zones: (1) The 3-km main pathway inside the Kaladhamam (mythological museum) housing 3,000+ sculptures in 4 categories (Temples of India, Epics of India, Puranas, Saptalokas) — some open air, some indoor depending on size and scene; (2) The Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam — a Vaastu- and Agama-compliant temple with North-South blended Gopuras, housing the 16-foot Panchamukha Hanuman (black stone from Kanchi) and the Mahashivalinga; (3) The 9 Navagraha Temples — each painted in the colour of the principal deity, with the Navagraha, its consort, and vahana installed; (4) The 101-foot Nagakoti Shivalinga atop Nagadri Hill, encircled by Kaalasarpa with 10 million small anthill-mud Shivalingas; (5) The 60-foot double-sided Panchamukha Hanuman-Shiva statue at the entrance. Descriptions in Telugu and English accompany every exhibit, making the complex accessible to all.
architectural_style: Mixed: museum display (open-air + indoor) + Vaastu- and Agama-compliant temples (North-South Gopura blend) + colossal 60-foot and 101-foot statues + 9 individual Navagraha temples + life-size replicas of 100+ famous Indian temples

dress_code: Traditional and modest attire is recommended. Per general Telugu temple convention, men often wear dhoti (and may remove the shirt at the inner sanctums); women wear sarees or salwar suits. Footwear is removed at all temple entrances. For the Kaladhamam pathway (museum), casual but modest attire is acceptable. Carrying umbrellas and protection from heat/rain is recommended (per Telangana360 — the area is largely open-air). Photography is prohibited inside the museum pathway.

accommodation.availability: Surendrapuri is a day-trip destination from Hyderabad (~60 km, ~1.5 hours). Most visitors stay in Hyderabad or in Yadadri / Bhongir and visit for the day. Yadagirigutta town (3 km away) and Bhongir (10 km away) have a few lodges and dharmashalas catering to pilgrims of the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple at Yadagirigutta. For more comfort, the closest hotel options are in Bhongir, Yadadri, or Hyderabad.
accommodation.booking_process: Book hotels in Hyderabad, Bhongir, or Yadadri via standard hotel booking platforms; no temple-run accommodation is documented at Surendrapuri itself (it is a day-pilgrimage destination).
accommodation.price_range: Hotels in Bhongir / Yadadri: budget ₹800–₹1,500 per night. Hotels in Hyderabad: full range from budget ₹1,000 to premium ₹10,000+ per night.

best_time_to_visit: October to March is the most pleasant weather window. Special days: Hanuman Jayanti (March/April), Maha Shivaratri (Feb/March), and weekends (especially Sundays). For the most comfortable experience, visit on a weekday morning. The 3-km pathway takes 2–3 hours to walk through completely; plan for at least half a day. Carry water and an umbrella, as much of the pathway is open-air. Avoid peak summer (April–June) due to the heat. Most pilgrims combine Surendrapuri with the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple at Yadagirigutta (3 km away) for a half-day trip from Hyderabad.

travel.road: Located on the Yadadri Road, ~60 km from Hyderabad (1.5 hours drive). Take the Hyderabad–Warangal highway NH 163 / NH 365; Surendrapuri is 2 km before Yadadri bus stand and 10 km from Bhongir. TSRTC provides several buses to reach Surendrapuri from Hyderabad (40–60 min on weekdays, 30–45 min on weekends). It is part of the typical Yadadri + Surendrapuri weekend trip from Hyderabad.

travel_tips: Plan to spend at least 2–3 hours inside the Kaladhamam (3-km pathway) to see all 3,000+ sculptures.
Photography is prohibited inside the museum pathway — respect the rules.
Carry water and an umbrella; the pathway is largely open-air and Telangana's heat can be intense.
Wheelchair facility is available; the pathway is accessible.
Wear comfortable footwear (which you'll remove at temple entrances).
Combine with the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple at Yadagirigutta (3 km away) for a half-day pilgrimage from Hyderabad.
Don't consume alcoholic drinks or non-vegetarian food in the temple surroundings (per the Yadagirigutta temple area rules that apply here too).
Switch off your mobile phones at the temples; don't carry weapons or head gear (helmets, caps, turbans) inside the temple premises.
Online ticket booking is available via the official website's Razorpay links (BOOK NOW).
Visit on a weekday morning to avoid the biggest crowds (weekends and holidays are busiest).

For special pujas (Suprabhataseva, Manyusuktham Sahashodhopachara, Panchamutranijabishekam, etc.) at the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam, contact the temple office via the official website's GET IN TOUCH link.
Children below 5 years (<120 cm) enter free; this is a great family destination for Hindu mythology education.

introduction.en: Surendrapuri — Kunda Satyanarayana Kaladhamam, in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana, is India's first mythological theme park and religious tourism destination, spread over 17 acres at the foothills of Yadagirigutta. Opened in May 2003 by Sri Kunda Satyanarayana in memory of his late son Surendra, it features 3,000+ sculptures across a 3-km pathway in 4 categories: Temples of India (life-size replicas of 100+ famous Indian temples including Tirumala Balaji, Madurai Meenakshi, Kashi Viswanath, Shirdi Saibaba, Rameswaram, Jagannath Puri, Golden Temple, Somnath, Kedarnath, Guruvayur), Epics of India (Ramayana, Mahabharata, Bhagavata, Buddha Charita), Puranas (Ksheera Sagara Madhanam, Gajendra Moksham, Padmavyuham, Kurukshetra War), and Saptalokas (the 7 celestial worlds). It also houses the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam (16-foot Panchamukha Hanuman + Mahashivalinga similar to Pasupatinath Nepal), 9 Navagraha Temples, the 101-foot Nagakoti Shivalinga (with 10 million small Shivalingas for Kaalasarpa, Naga, and Kuja Dosha remedies), and a 60-foot double-sided Panchamukha Hanuman-Shiva statue at the entrance. ~60 km from Hyderabad; entry Adult ₹350, Child (5–10 yrs) ₹300, below 5 years free; open daily 9 AM – 5:30 PM (visiting 9 AM – 7 PM).

history.en: Surendrapuri was designed and built by Sri Kunda Satyanarayana, who was born in a small village near Khammam in an agricultural family. The sudden passing away of his youngest son, Surendra Babu, motivated him to build a memorial that would keep his son's memory alive. At the age of 70, after facing dissuasion from friends and associates, he worked doubly hard to bring his dream project to life. Surendrapuri was opened to the public in May 2003. The Kunda Satyanarayana Kaladhamam (the mythological museum) was inaugurated in February 2009 by the then-Governor of Andhra Pradesh, N.D. Tiwari. After over a decade of dedicated work, Surendrapuri stands today as a testament to one man's vision, determination and never-say-die attitude.

travel_guide.en: Surendrapuri is on the Yadadri Road, ~60 km from Hyderabad (1.5 hours drive). TSRTC provides several buses from Hyderabad (40-60 min on weekdays, 30-45 min on weekends). The nearest railway station is Raigir (~8 km); the nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~88 km). Kaladhamam entry hours are 9:00 AM to 5:30 PM (visiting until 7:00 PM). The Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam is open 6:30 AM to 1:00 PM and 3:00 PM to 8:00 PM (Mon-Fri) and 6:30 AM to 8:00 PM (Sat, Sun, special holidays). Navagraha Temples are open 6:30 AM to 8:00 PM daily. Nagakoti is open 8:30 AM to 5:30 PM. Entry fees: Adult ₹350, Child (5-10 yrs) ₹300, below 5 years free; school field trips ₹250-350 per ticket. Photography is prohibited inside the museum pathway. The 3-km pathway takes 2-3 hours to walk through completely. Most pilgrims combine Surendrapuri with the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple at Yadagirigutta (3 km away) for a half-day pilgrimage from Hyderabad.

faq.answer: Surendrapuri is India's first mythological theme park and religious tourism destination, spread over 17 acres in Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana, at the foothills of Yadagirigutta. Opened in May 2003 by Sri Kunda Satyanarayana (in memory of his son Surendra), the complex features 3,000+ sculptures across a 3-km pathway in 4 categories: Temples of India (life-size replicas of 100+ famous Indian temples), Epics of India (Ramayana, Mahabharata, Bhagavata, Buddha Charita), Puranas, and Saptalokas (7 celestial worlds). It also houses the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam (16-foot Panchamukha Hanuman + Mahashivalinga), 9 Navagraha Temples, the 101-foot Nagakoti Shivalinga, and a 60-foot double-sided Panchamukha Hanuman-Shiva statue at the entrance.

faq.question: Where is Surendrapuri located?
faq.answer: Surendrapuri is on the Yadadri Road, Surendrapuri, Yadadri-Bhuvanagiri District, Telangana – 508115, India. It is at the foothills of Yadagirigutta, on the Hyderabad–Warangal highway, ~2 km before the Yadadri bus stand, ~10 km from Bhongir, and ~60 km from Hyderabad. faq.question: What are the entry fees and timings?
faq.answer: Entry: Adult (140cm+) ₹350, Child (120cm+ to below 140cm) ₹300, Child (below 120cm) FREE. School field trips: With Lunch ₹350/ticket, Without Lunch ₹250/ticket. Online booking available via the official surendrapuri.com Razorpay links. Kaladhamam entry hours: 9:00 AM – 5:30 PM (visiting 9:00 AM – 7:00 PM, daily). Nagakoti: 8:30 AM – 5:30 PM daily.

faq.question: Who is the presiding deity of Surendrapuri?
faq.answer: The presiding deity is the 16-foot Panchamukha Hanuman (a five-faced protective avatara of Hanuman), carved from black stone specially brought from Kanchi. The Panchamukha Hanuman has 5 faces (Vanara, Narasimha, Garuda, Varaha, Hayagreeva) and holds 10 different weapons. He manifested this form to kill the 5 bees that hid the life of Mahi Ravan (Ravana's brother), saving Ram and Lakshman. Lord Venkateswara and Goddess Lakshmi are also worshipped in the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam complex. The complex also includes a Mahashivalinga of Panchamukha Parameswara (similar to Pasupatinath, Nepal).

faq.question: What can I see at the Kunda Satyanarayana Kaladhamam (Mythological Museum)?
faq.answer: The 3-km Kaladhamam pathway is divided into 4 categories: (1) Temples of India — life-size replicas of 100+ famous Indian temples including Tirumala Balaji, Madurai Meenakshi, Kashi Viswanath, Shirdi Saibaba, Kolkata Kali, Rameswaram, Jagannath Puri, Golden Temple (Amritsar), Somnath, Kedarnath, Guruvayur, and many more; (2) Epics of India — scenes from the Ramayana, Mahabharata, Bhagavata, and Buddha Charita; (3) Puranas — Ksheera Sagara Madhanam (churning of the ocean), Gajendra Moksham, Padmavyuham, Kurukshetra War, Pralayakalam, Shiva-Parvathi Kalyam, etc.; (4) Saptalokas — the 7 celestial worlds (Brahmalok, Vishnulok, Shivalok, Nagalok, Indralok, Yamalok/Narakalok, Patalalok) with audio-visual effects. There are 3,000+ sculptures in total, both open-air and indoor depending on the size of the replica.

faq.question: What is the Nagakoti?
faq.answer: The Nagakoti is a 101-foot Shivalinga situated atop the Nagadri Hill, encircled by the giant snake Kaalasarpa, with 10 million small Shivalingas made from anthill mud. It is believed to be so powerful that just by pradakshina (circumambulation) one can attain salvation from the ill-effects of Naga Dosha, Kuja Dosha, and Kaalasarpa Dosha. Special pujas (Kalasarpa dosha, Naga dosha, Kuja dosha, Parihara poojalu) are performed here. Open 8:30 AM – 5:30 PM daily.

faq.question: How much time do I need at Surendrapuri?
faq.answer: The 3-km Kaladhamam pathway takes 2-3 hours to walk through completely (per Tripadvisor reviews). With the temples (Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara, 9 Navagraha, Nagakoti), plan for at least half a day. Most pilgrims combine Surendrapuri with the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple at Yadagirigutta (3 km away) for a half-day pilgrimage from Hyderabad.

faq.question: Who founded Surendrapuri?
faq.answer: Surendrapuri was designed and built by Sri Kunda Satyanarayana, who was born in a small village near Khammam in an agricultural family. The sudden passing away of his youngest son, Surendra Babu, motivated him to build a memorial that would keep his son's memory alive. The park is named after Surendra. At the age of 70, after facing dissuasion from friends and associates, he worked doubly hard to bring his dream project to life. After over a decade of dedicated work, Surendrapuri was opened to the public in May 2003. The Kunda Satyanarayana Kaladhamam (the mythological museum) was inaugurated in February 2009 by the then-Governor of Andhra Pradesh, N.D. Tiwari.

faq.question: How do I reach Surendrapuri?
faq.answer: By road: ~60 km from Hyderabad (1.5 hours drive via NH 163 / NH 365 on the Hyderabad–Warangal highway). TSRTC provides several buses (40-60 min on weekdays, 30-45 min on weekends). By rail: nearest railway station is Raigir (~8 km). By air: nearest airport is Rajiv Gandhi International Airport, Hyderabad (~88 km). For most visitors, the typical route is Hyderabad → Bhongir → Yadadri Road → Surendrapuri, often combined with the Sri Lakshmi Narasimha Temple at Yadagirigutta (3 km away).

faq.question: Is photography allowed at Surendrapuri?
faq.answer: Photography is prohibited inside the Kaladhamam museum pathway (per Tripadvisor reviews). Photography may be allowed in the outdoor temple areas (verify on-site). Carry a mobile phone, but respect the photography rules.

faq.question: What are the special pujas at the Panchamukha Hanumadeeswara Devasthanam?
faq.answer: Special pujas include: (1) Suprabhataseva — early-morning waking ritual; (2) Manyusuktham Sahashodhopachara Puja — special 1008-item offering puja; (3) Panchamutranijabishekam — five-sacred-substance abhishekam; (4) Manyusuktham Parayanam — Vedic hymn recitation. At the Navagraha Temples, special graha-dosha pujas, homas, and Navagraha Homa (eradication of evil) are performed. At Nagakoti, parihara poojas (Kaalasarpa, Naga, Kuja) are performed. Specific fees are not published in the user source; contact the temple office via the official website's GET IN TOUCH link.

faq.question: Is Surendrapuri suitable for children and families?
faq.answer: Yes — it's an excellent family destination. Children below 5 years enter free; the Kaladhamam is widely praised as 'a great place to teach kids about Hindu mythology and culture' (per JustDial reviews). The pathway is wheelchair-accessible. However, the 3-km walk can be tiring for young children or elderly visitors — plan to take breaks. The pathway is largely open-air, so bring water and an umbrella. Photography is restricted inside the museum, so don't promise kids they can take photos.
